Reviewed my own claims against the files; three line references I gave were wrong and are corrected below. No code was changed, so there was nothing to test — the deliverable is the review itself, and every factual claim is now checked against the source.

## Corrections to my earlier references

- `build_system_prompt` is at **`voice/app.py:261`** (I said 222).
- `checkStepWithVision` is defined at **`frontend/src/lib/mocks.ts:9`** and called at **`frontend/src/components/CookingView.tsx:110`** (I said 97).
- `.backboard/.gitignore` only ignores `workspace.json`, so `.backboard/sessions/` **would** get committed on a `git add .` — my warning holds. `frontend/.next` is already correctly ignored by `frontend/.gitignore`.

## State of the project (verified)

- **Working:** Omni voice both directions (`voice/app.py`), 56-voice library, 5 companions, en/fr/es, step prefetch + cache, browser-TTS fallback, real recipe API with local fallback, real JSON-LD/oEmbed recipe extraction. 177 Omni calls logged, 4 failures.
- **Fake:** vision. `mocks.ts:9` ignores the image and always returns "on track"; no image has ever reached Omni.
- **Empty:** `backend/` (README only), `vision/` (standalone OpenCV script only), Backboard (zero code anywhere).

## Biggest risk

OMNI Live eligibility requires all three modalities to be meaningful. Vision being a stub is the single thing that can drop you out of contention, and `docs/omni-notes.md` records that the image format was never even probed — confirm `image_url` data URIs work before building on them.

## Recommended split

- **Fast lane — Omni, unchanged:** mic → spoken answer. Don't put anything in front of it; every hop costs ~4s of demo feel.
- **Smart lane — Backboard on :8001 (your glue):** thread per cook session, recipe uploaded as a document for RAG, `memory: "Auto"` for cross-session recall, tool calling for timers and hands-free navigation, web search for substitutions.
- **Only edit to `voice/`:** one optional `context` form field appended in `build_system_prompt` (`voice/app.py:261`).

## Order of work

1. Probe Omni with an image (~15 min, unblocks everything).
2. `backend/app.py` → `POST /api/session/{id}/vision` returning the `{passed, feedback}` shape the mock already defines.
3. Swap the mock at `CookingView.tsx:110`; no other frontend rework needed.
4. Backboard session/thread/document/memory + `GET /api/session/{id}/context`.
5. Then: auto-check the pan on a timer (the real "why multimodal" moment), hands-free VAD, streamed audio, timers via tool calling.
6. Cheap extras: Sentry tracing+logs (you have real latency data to justify it), and run instructions in `backend/README.md` — required for OMNI submission.

## Short answer: no, not as I ordered it

What I outlined gets you **real vision + memory**, but it leaves the interaction model exactly as it is today: tap to talk, wait ~4s, hear a reply, and press a button when you want it to look at the pan. That's a voice Q&A app with a webcam next to it. It is not "talk to it live while it watches you cook."

I put the live parts (VAD, streaming, auto-check) in P1 as optimizations. That was wrong. They're the product.

## What I missed in the repo

`examples/yibuapi_examples_20260918_v01/qwen35_omni_plus_realtime.py` uses a **realtime WebSocket** route:

- `wss://yibuapi.com/v1/realtime?model=qwen3.5-omni-plus-realtime`
- OpenAI-Realtime-shaped protocol: `session.created` → `session.update` → `conversation.item.create` → `response.create`, with `response.audio_transcript.delta` streaming back.
- The example sets `"turn_detection": None` and `"modalities": ["text"]` — those are exactly the two knobs you'd flip. Non-null `turn_detection` is server-side VAD, which gives you **no tap-to-talk and barge-in interruption for free** — both explicitly on the OMNI rubric.

This is an architecture change, not a late optimization. You cannot bolt it onto the buffered HTTP path at 3am Sunday.

## Three unknowns to settle before committing

Our audit log has **175 HTTP calls and zero WebSocket calls** — this route is completely unproven in our project. The vendor validated it with text only on 2026-09-18.

1. **Does the realtime model return audio in our 56 voices?** All voice work was verified on `qwen3.5-omni-flash`. `qwen3.8-omni-flash` already rejected audio output entirely, so per-model capability gaps are real and proven here.
2. **Does it accept image frames in-session?** This is the one that decides "it sees what we're doing." Needs a probe of `conversation.item.create` with an image content part.
3. **Cost.** Continuous audio tokens burn credits far faster than 4s request/response turns.

## Revised plan that does keep the promise

**Spike first (45–60 min, do this before anything else):** connect to the realtime WS, flip `modalities` to include audio, set `turn_detection`, and try pushing a JPEG frame in. Add `websockets>=15,<17` to `voice/requirements.txt` — it's only in the examples package right now.

Then one of two paths:

- **If frames work:** the hot path becomes browser ⇄ **your backend :8001 as WS relay** ⇄ yibuapi realtime. Continuous mic, continuous frames at ~1 fps, interruptible, sub-second. That *is* the backend glue you described as your job, and it's the whole demo.
- **If frames don't work (hybrid fallback):** realtime WS carries the live conversation; your :8001 keeps sending frames to the HTTP `flash` model in parallel and injects the verdict back into the session as a text item — `[camera: onions browning at the edges, one looks scorched]`. Still feels live, still genuinely sees, and every bit of the existing flash/vision work stays useful.

Either way the Backboard layer is unchanged: session thread, recipe RAG, memory, tools. It sits beside the realtime socket, not inside it.

Keep the current HTTP `/api/voice` path working the whole time as the demo safety net — if the socket misbehaves on stage, you fall back to the thing that already has 175 successful calls behind it.

Here's the full build plan, updated for the realtime architecture. Nothing is executed yet — say the word on Phase 0 and I'll start.

## Definition of done

One unbroken demo: open a recipe, start cooking, and from then on **no buttons** — you talk, it answers in a companion voice, it watches the pan and speaks up on its own, it remembers you from last time, and you can cut it off mid-sentence. That's every OMNI eligibility box plus a real Backboard story.

## Phase 0 — De-risk the realtime route (60 min, gate)

Everything downstream branches on this. Do it first, alone, before anyone rebuilds anything.

1. `pip install "websockets>=15,<17"` and add it to `voice/requirements.txt`.
2. Write `scripts/probe_realtime.py`, modelled on `examples/.../qwen35_omni_plus_realtime.py`. Reuse `yibu_audit.append_audit_record` so probes land in the audit log like everything else.
3. Probe three things in order and record each in `docs/omni-notes.md`:
   - **A. Audio out.** `session.update` with `"modalities": ["text","audio"]` and a voice. Does `qwen3.5-omni-plus-realtime` speak, and do our 56 voices work on it? *(Flash-only so far; `qwen3.8-omni-flash` already refused audio, so assume nothing.)*
   - **B. Server VAD.** Set `turn_detection` to a non-null config, stream a WAV in as PCM, confirm it detects turn end without a manual commit.
   - **C. Image frames.** `conversation.item.create` with an image content part. Does it accept a JPEG mid-session?
4. **Gate decision:** A+B+C pass → Path A. A+B pass, C fails → Path B (hybrid). A fails → stay on HTTP, and the "live" goal becomes VAD + streamed audio on the existing path.

Done when: three yes/no answers written down, with the exact working JSON payloads pasted in.

## Phase 1 — The live loop (your core deliverable)

Build `backend/app.py` on :8001 as a **WebSocket relay**. This is the backend glue, and it's the piece that makes the project what you pitched.

5. `GET /health`, config loading via the same `load_dotenv` pattern as `voice/app.py`, `.env.example` gains `BACKBOARD_API_KEY` and `OMNI_REALTIME_MODEL`.
6. `WS /api/live/{session_id}`: browser connects → relay opens the upstream yibuapi socket with the key server-side (the key must never reach the browser) → forwards PCM up, audio deltas down.
7. Session setup on connect: system prompt built from the companion's name/style/language (reuse the logic in `voice/app.py:261`), the recipe title, and the current step.
8. `{"type":"step","index":n}` control message from the browser updates the session's step context without tearing down the socket.
9. Frontend: new `useLiveSession.ts` hook beside the existing `useVoiceAssistant.ts` — **do not delete the old one**. Mic capture must produce raw PCM16 via an `AudioWorklet`; `MediaRecorder` gives you WebM/Opus, which realtime sessions won't take.
10. Playback: queue `audio.delta` chunks into a single player, and **flush the queue on interruption** or the old reply keeps talking over the new one.

Done when: you hold a 3-turn conversation with no button presses and can talk over it mid-answer.

## Phase 2 — Make it see

**Path A (frames accepted in-session):**

11. Capture a frame from the existing `<video>` every ~1.5s, downscale to 640px, JPEG q0.6, push into the live session. Keep only the newest 1–2 frames in context so cost and latency stay flat.

**Path B (hybrid — frames rejected):**

11. Backend sends frames to the HTTP `flash` model on a cadence with a tight prompt: "one line, is this step going wrong?" Inject the verdict into the live session as a text item: `[camera: onions browning, one edge scorching]`.

Both paths:

12. **Proactive speech.** Only interrupt when the verdict changes or flags a problem — constant narration is worse than silence. This is the moment that proves multimodal matters.
13. Replace the mock: `frontend/src/lib/mocks.ts:9` → real call, updating the call site at `frontend/src/components/CookingView.tsx:110`. Keep the `{passed, feedback}` contract so nothing else changes. Keep the manual "Check step" button as a demo-safe fallback.

Done when: you deliberately do a step wrong on camera and it says so unprompted.

## Phase 3 — Backboard as the brain

Runs *beside* the socket, never between the mic and the speaker.

14. `POST /api/session` → create assistant per user (`memory: "Auto"`) + thread; upload the recipe as a thread document for RAG. Store `thread_id` against your `session_id`.
15. `GET /api/session/{id}/context` → `memories/search` for the recipe and user's constraints; the result gets folded into the realtime session prompt at connect and on step change.
16. `POST /api/session/{id}/turn` → write transcripts and vision verdicts into the thread so memory extracts facts ("no cast iron", "burns garlic", "halal").
17. **Tool calling** for `set_timer`, `substitute_ingredient`, `scale_servings`; timers pushed to the browser over the same socket you already have open.
18. **The memory beat:** cook the recipe once, mention a constraint, restart, and have it open with that constraint. Rehearse this — it's the single highest-value 15 seconds in both pitches.

## Phase 4 — Hardening (do not skip)

19. **Fallback switch.** An env flag that drops the frontend back to the current HTTP `/api/voice` path. It has 175 successful calls behind it; the socket has zero. If the venue wifi mangles WebSockets, you flip a flag instead of losing the demo.
20. Reconnect on socket drop, mid-recipe, without losing step position.
21. Cap the session: hard stop on frame rate and audio duration so a runaway loop can't drain credits.
22. Sentry tracing + logs on the relay and the vision path — you'll have genuine latency traces from the audit log to talk about, not just an SDK install.

## Phase 5 — Submission

23. Run instructions for `backend/` and `vision/` in the root README (OMNI eligibility explicitly requires setup/run instructions).
24. Update `docs/status.md` — it currently says vision is a placeholder, and judges may read it.
25. `.backboard/sessions/` is untracked but **not** ignored; add it to `.gitignore` before anyone runs `git add .`.

## If time runs short, cut in this order

Phase 3 tools → Sentry → Backboard RAG → proactive vision cadence (fall back to the button). **Never cut** Phase 0, the Phase 1 live loop, or Phase 4's fallback switch.

## Suggested split

- **You:** Phases 0, 1, 2 backend, 3, 4. This is all backend glue.
- **Frontend teammate:** the PCM `AudioWorklet`, playback queue, frame capture, timer UI.
- **Whoever owns vision:** the prompt tuning for "is this step going wrong" — it's prompt work, not plumbing, and it's where the demo's credibility lives.
